chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah for six circuits, while he thought they were seven. He mentioned that after he had become free from Ihram and had intercourse with his wives, he realized he had only performed six circuits. So he said: 'He must slaughter a cow, slaughter it, and perform one additional circuit.'
And there is no harm if a person runs between As-Safa and Al-Marwah without Wudu, and Wudu is better.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the two hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.بَقَرَةٌ: A cow (used here as the specific expiation)
key_terms.سَعَى: Ran/Walked briskly (referring to the ritual of Sa'i)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for missing one circuit during Sa'i in Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific expiation (Kaffarah) of slaughtering a cow for a pilgrim who mistakenly completes only six circuits of Sa'i, highlighting the severity of the error in the ritual's completeness. The hadith further clarifies the juristic distinction between obligatory purity (Wudu) and recommended purity, noting that while Wudu is superior, Sa'i remains valid without it, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ritual flexibility in non-prayer acts of worship. This ruling underscores the principle that doubt in the number of circuits requires verification and correction to ensure the validity of Hajj or Umrah.
